findings.reason: The protected source is the standard bottom-up interval minimax dynamic program. It initializes zero-cost singleton intervals, evaluates every first guess against the worse shorter branch, retains the minimum guarantee, and fills states in dependency order. The implementation is clear and interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 375 and its Python getMoneyAmount surface. The Reference preserves the hidden-number game, payment only for wrong guesses, minimum guaranteed worst-case budget, all three source examples and explanations, the first strategy tree, and the n-at-most-200 constraint.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064636219. Its padded cost table, interval-length order, boundaries, full pivot scan, minimax candidate, best update, table write, and final lookup are exactly the protected app-local algorithm apart from the required LeetCode wrapper.

The legal interval-DP tiers use n values 8, 16, and 32 and span 4x while evaluating nontrivial minimax tables. The current source passes all 11 executions at +0.01 relative growth and 1.01x; correct per-pivot enumeration of every hidden target passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +0.95 and 14.16x.

The Approach accurately defines interval state, derives the guess-plus-worse-branch transition, proves the adversarial lower bound and achievable strategy, gives the dependency order, and states O(n^3) time with O(n^2) space. Its expected-cost and final-correct-guess distinctions are precise.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including all three source examples and complete explanations, an independent text reconstruction of the first strategy diagram, every game and payment rule, and the sole source constraint.
